section.name: Subversion
section.p: All of the Apache Tomcat source code, documentation and this web site are managed under version control using Subversion. This page explains the structure of the Apache Tomcat Subversion repository. The page assumes you are familiar with the general Apache guidance for Subversion.
All Subversion links on this page use anonymous access.

section.name: Repository Structure
section.p:
The root of the repository is
http://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/tomcat.
Note: there is also ViewVC-powered web view of the repository.
The directories below this level are:

tr.td: Modules that are no longer maintained

The native source code for the Tomcat Connectors. This includes mod_jk, isapi and nsapi. The current code is in
/jk/trunk/.
The Apache Tomcat Maven Plugin source code and website.

The native source code for the Tomcat Native/APR Connector. The current code is in
/native/branches/1.1.x/ (1.1.x) and
/native/trunk/ (1.2.x).
An area where Tomcat committers can experiment with new ideas.
The Apache Taglibs source code and website.
Tags for the primary development branch. Mainly used for modules.
The primary development branch. Patches are committed here using Commit-then-Review and then voted on for porting to the release branches using Review-then-Commit.

section.name: Git Mirror
section.p: The Apache Software Foundation provides read-only Git mirrors for its projects. See http://git.apache.org/
Several notes for the users of Git:

ol.li: The Git repositories at http://git.apache.org/ and their clones at GitHub are only mirrors. The official code repository is the Subversion one, documented above.
To propose a patch, please follow general patch submission guidelines, documented on the Bug Database page.
